name: Solid orange with the white BI tail, 747-127 N601BN (1979)
description: The scheme 747-127 N601BN, 'Big Orange', still wore in 1979 (the 1971 scheme of Braniff's first 747, which it kept to the end): the body and tailplane a deep orange, belly included, the fin and rudder white, with a large 'BI' in orange-red on the fin and a small US flag above it. 'BRANIFF INTERNATIONAL' in white forward-leaning extended capitals over the forward main-deck windows. Bare polished nacelles, gray wings.

sources.title: Yesterday's Airlines: The Elegance Campaign, Braniff's Ultra Look
sources.note: Evidence only: Ultra unveiled 17 July 1978; eight darker colors (terra cotta, Perseus green, Mercury blue, metallic blue, light Corvette blue, chocolate brown, burgundy, sparkling burgundy); the 25 727s delivered from April 1978 in Ultra, only 12 older 727s repainted; all but two DC-8-62s repainted; the 747s in an orange version with a solid orange belly, except N601BN; a mix of Ultra and Flying Colors to the end in 1982.

titles.style: Braniff International's 1970s lettering in white: heavy, extended, forward-leaning capitals with square counters, over the forward main-deck windows.

notes: Measured 2026-11-24 for ghost flights on N601BN (June 1979, right side; fitted to shapes/B744-passenger.json by the nose, doors 1 and 5 and the crown and belly, within 10 px; the fin's place in the fit is poor, so the 'BI' and flag are placed by eye as shares of the fin's own outline). The title, re-measured 2026-11-25 by doors 1 to 3 and the window rows (and on the September 1981 photo), runs from 11.1 to 27.2 m back, its thin extended capitals about 0.5 m tall (0.47 m and 0.56 m on the two photos), the baseline 1.38 m above the centerline, well under the upper deck's three windows (it had been drawn 1.65 m tall). Drawn on the 747-100/-200 shape (shapes/B742.json: the short upper deck, no winglets). The white fin and 'BI' are still there in September 1981 (Gatwick); Yesterday's Airlines says it never got the Ultra colors. Colors read off slides, approximate.

B742.note: The fin's large 'BI' and flag were placed on the 747's fin (N601BN, 1979). So they're the 747's: on another type the scheme keeps its orange body, white fin and title but no fin marks, which would crowd a fin of another shape.

logos.description: Braniff International's 'BI' in orange-red: two heavy, extended, square-cornered capitals with small square counters, low on the white fin.
A small US flag above the 'BI', the canton forward.
